en.title: Non-Overlapping Zero-Sum Triplets
en.description:
Given an integer array A. You may choose several contiguous segments of length exactly 3; the sum of each segment must be 0, and no two chosen segments may share an array position. Find the maximum number of segments you can choose. You cannot reorder the array, and you cannot pick three numbers that are not contiguous.

This problem uses the standard input/output format compiled by CSWork; the algorithmic rules correspond to the source problem, and the examples and test data are written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100); the second line contains n integers A[i] (−100 ≤ A[i] ≤ 100).
en.explanation: In example 1, you can choose [1,0,−1] at positions 1..3 and then [0,0,0] at positions 4..6, so the answer is 2. Indices start from 0.
hints: Scan from left to right for the first triplet with sum 0; once it is chosen, skip its three positions entirely; otherwise move one position to the right.
